where: Section 1, paragraph on responsibility ("Other cells are trained as no-object")
problem: Read literally, this says every cell except the responsible one gets a no-object target for this object. A cell can hold the centre of a second object, and then it is a positive cell for that object. A student may think such a cell is wrongly punished.
fix: "Only the cell whose area contains the object centre is responsible for that object. Every other cell gets zero objectness for it; a cell that holds another object's centre is positive for that other object."

where: Section 1, confidence definition, and worked example 1 part (d)
problem: The chapter defines confidence as Pr(object) × IoU with the truth box and then uses 0.8 from the IoU with the truth as if it were available at test time. At test time there is no truth box; the network outputs its own confidence, trained towards that product. Without this line a student may think IoU with ground truth is computed during inference.
fix: Add: "The product is the training target. At test time the network outputs its own predicted confidence, so no ground truth is needed."

problem: The class score is called a plain "class probability", but YOLO's C class numbers are conditional probabilities, Pr(Class_i | Object). This is exactly why multiplying by confidence gives a valid per-class score; without it the multiplication step looks arbitrary.
fix: State that the cell gives C conditional class probabilities Pr(Class_i | Object), and the test score for a box is confidence × Pr(Class_i | Object).
